newsitem.title: GERMANY: German church bomb shatters Christmas Eve service.
newsitem.headline: German church bomb shatters Christmas Eve service.

text.p: A Christmas tree next to the alter glowed brightly in the front of the South Sindlingen Protestant Church, standing unscathed by the horror that had erupted in the packed midnight service hours earlier.
There was an ominous silence on this holy night.
It was a freezing cold cloudless night that local residents hoped to round off by singing Christmas songs at the church with their neighbours.
But the "muffled bang" that exploded in the back of the church that was crowded with 70 people was followed by screams of panic and pain.
It took only a few moments for the sirens of police, ambulance and firefighters to pierce the midnight quiet of the sleepy western German city.
"The fire department found a scene of shock and panic upon their arrival," said police spokesman Manfred Feist.
Criminal investigators sifting through the church shattered by a suspected suicide bomber early on Wednesday morning were confronted by an grisly Christmas Eve nightmare.

Three women were killed and 10 critically injured in a horrifying bomb blast that turned the third to last row in the small church in this unremarkable Frankfurt working class district into a jumble of splintered pine.

Small pieces of human flesh were splattered on the church's white walls, blood-covered body parts were scattered on the floor and many pair of gloves lay abandoned on the floor -- silent testimony to the panicked dash to the exits after the powerful bomb detonated.
"That is the brain of one victim," said a police officer searching the crime scene for clues that may help investigators unravel the mystery shrouding the attack.
Ruling out a guerrilla attack, police said they were baffled about the possible motive for the bombing.
"I have no idea who could have done such a thing on a day like this," Frankfurt police chief Wolfhard Hoffmann said.
One woman who belongs to the church said that there had been some tensions among some members of the community in recent weeks.
"But I cannot possibly imagine that those misunderstandings could lead to something like this," said the woman, who declined to give her name.

Police and emergency workers were still carrying pieces of bodies out of the church in plastic bags several hours after the attack, which attracted dozens of journalists, photographers and television crews.
Other investigators searching for clues were knocking on the doors of nearby houses.
